Model spray combustion of liquid dodecane in a cylindrical combustion chamber using OpenFOAM's reactingParcelFoam solver.

The computational domain is a 2D axisymmetric wedge representing a cylinder 0.2 m long in the axial direction and 0.1 m in diameter.

Use a 5 degree wedge with symmetry axis along the centerline, with 100 cells in the axial direction and 50 cells in the radial direction.

Set the operating pressure to 101325 Pa and initialize the entire chamber uniformly at p = 101325 Pa and T = 800 K.

Set the inlet co-flow air velocity to U = (10 0 0) m/s, temperature to 800 K, pressure to 101325 Pa, and species mass fractions to O2 = 0.233 and N2 = 0.767.

Set the outlet boundary condition to totalPressure at 101325 Pa with appropriate inlet-outlet velocity and temperature conditions.

Use the k-epsilon turbulence model with standard wall functions for the chamber walls.

Use the PaSR combustion model and define a two-step global reaction mechanism for n-dodecane with janaf thermodynamics.

Set up the spray as a cone injection model in constant/sprayCloudProperties with a mass flow rate of 0.002 kg/s.

Set the initial droplet temperature to 300 K and the initial droplet injection velocity to 10 m/s in the axial direction.

Use a Rosin-Rammler droplet size distribution with a mean diameter of 50e-6 m and define a reasonable minimum and maximum droplet diameter and spread parameter, for example min diameter 10e-6 m, max diameter 150e-6 m, and spread parameter n = 2.0.

Set the droplet heat and mass transfer model to RanzMarshall and the drag model to standard.

Initialize the gas phase species in the chamber as air at the specified composition, O2 = 0.233 and N2 = 0.767, with no dodecane vapor initially present.

Set the cone angle of the dodecane spray injection to 30 degrees as a reasonable default, with the spray directed along the positive axial direction and positioned at the center of the inlet.
